chemistry-killer-09.goal: Analyze the principles of Conservation of Mass and Definite Proportions and deduce the correct conclusion under given conditions.
chemistry-killer-09.material: At constant temperature and pressure, gases A and B react to form gas C in $\mathrm{aA(g) + bB(g) \rightarrow cC(g)}$. 20 mL of A and 60 mL of B react exactly to give 40 mL of C. The molecular mass of A is 28 and that of B is 2. A 100 mL mixture of A and B (average molecular mass 12.4) is reacted completely at the same temperature and pressure. How many times the density of the gas mixture before the reaction is the density of the gas mixture after the reaction?
chemistry-killer-09.thinking.0: Conservation of Mass and Definite Proportions
chemistry-killer-09.s.s1.prompt: At constant temperature and pressure, gases A and B react to form gas C in $\mathrm{aA(g) + bB(g) \rightarrow cC(g)}$. 20 mL of A and 60 mL of B react exactly to give 40 mL of C. The molecular mass of A is 28 and that of B is 2. A 100 mL mixture of A and B (average molecular mass 12.4) is reacted completely at the same temperature and pressure. How many times the density of the gas mixture before the reaction is the density of the gas mixture after the reaction?
chemistry-killer-09.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: Volume ratio A:B:C = 20:60:40 = 1:3:2, i.e. $\mathrm{A + 3B \rightarrow 2C}$.
Step 2: In the 100 mL mixture let A = x mL: (28x + 2(100 - x))/100 = 12.4, so 26x + 200 = 1240 and x = 40 mL. A = 40 mL, B = 60 mL.
Step 3: All 60 mL of B reacts, using 20 mL of A and giving 40 mL of C. After the reaction: A 20 mL + C 40 mL = 60 mL.
Step 4: Mass is conserved (check: before 40 x 28 + 60 x 2 = 1240; C has molecular mass (28 + 3 x 2)/2 = 17, after 20 x 28 + 40 x 17 = 1240). At the same T and P, density = mass/volume, so after/before = 100/60 = 5/3.
Answer: 5/3 (a). (Wrong options: 3/5 inverts the ratio; 1 uses mass conservation but ignores the volume change; 5/4 wrongly leaves 40 mL of A, giving a total of 80 mL.)
chemistry-killer-09.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
chemistry-killer-09.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
chemistry-killer-09.s.s1.hint.0: At the same temperature and pressure, gas density is proportional to average molecular mass, and mass is conserved, so the density ratio is the inverse of the volume ratio. Use the average molecular mass to find the volumes of A and B.
chemistry-killer-09.s.s1.hint.1: 28x + 2(100 - x) = 12.4 x 100 gives x = 40 mL (A) and B = 60 mL. With A:B:C = 1:3:2, all 60 mL of B reacts using 20 mL of A and forming 40 mL of C, leaving 20 mL of A, so the total after is 60 mL.
